title: A full automorphism flag with a simultaneous finite coefficient model
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $E_0\subset\Omega$ be finite over $K$ [def-pc-field-tower], and let $V_0$ be a finite-dimensional $E_0$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace, def-weil-vector-space-dimension] with a specified basis $c_1,\ldots,c_d$. Let $F_0:V_0\xrightarrow{\sim}V_0$ be an $E_0$-linear automorphism and use vector-space scalar extension [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] to put $V=V_0\otimes_{E_0}\Omega$ and $F=F_0\otimes1$. There exist a finite intermediate extension $E_0\subset E\subset\Omega$, an $E$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $V_E=V_0\otimes_{E_0}E$, a full flag $0=W_{0,E}\subset W_{1,E}\subset\cdots\subset W_{d,E}=V_E$, and scalars $\alpha_j\in E^\times$ for $1\le j\le d$ with the following properties.
One has $W_{j,E}=\operatorname{span}_E(b_1,\ldots,b_j)$ and $\dim_E W_{j,E}=j$. Both $F_E=F_0\otimes1$ and $F_E^{-1}$ preserve every $W_{j,E}$; their restrictions and their induced quotient maps are mutually inverse, and $F_E$ acts on $W_{j,E}/W_{j-1,E}$ by $\alpha_j$. The change-of-basis matrices $B,B^{-1}$ from $c$ to $b$, and the matrices of $F_E,F_E^{-1}$ in $b$, all have entries in this same $E$; the latter two matrices are upper triangular. Every inclusion and quotient projection and the adapted bases of the short exact sequences $0\to W_{j-1,E}\to W_{j,E}\to W_{j,E}/W_{j-1,E}\to0$ are defined over $E$.
After scalar extension to $\Omega$, these data give a full $F$-invariant flag in $V$ with the same dimensions and nonzero quotient scalars; the displayed sequences remain exact and the restrictions and quotient operators remain invertible. The assertion allows repeated eigenvalues and nonzero off-diagonal entries. If $d=0$, the basis is empty and the flag has only its zero endpoint, with no quotient conditions.

proof.text: Extend c and F₀ to Ω by Basis.baseChange and LinearEquiv.baseChange. The scalar-extended basis has size d, including d = 0. Use Module.End.exists_basis_isUpperTriangular_toMatrix to obtain a triangular basis a over Ω, reindexed by Fin d.

Let S be the finite range of the d² coordinates of a in c.baseChange Ω, and let E = IntermediateField.adjoin E₀ S. Algebra.IsAlgebraic.tower_top gives algebraicity over E₀; IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin proves E/E₀ finite. Define candidate vectors v by exactly these coordinates in c.baseChange E. Their canonical images in Ω ⊗ V₀ are a. Independence descends through that E-linear map by LinearIndependent.of_comp and restrict_scalars'; the cardinality equals finrank, so basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank' gives the desired basis b. The tensor tower isomorphism carries b.baseChange Ω to a.

The matrix of a base-changed map in the base-changed basis is the entrywise algebraMap image of its original matrix. LinearMap.baseChange_baseChange identifies the conjugation by cancelBaseChange. Thus triangularity over Ω reflects to E by injectivity of algebraMap. Basis.toMatrix_mul_toMatrix_flip supplies both change-of-basis inverse identities. The operator and inverse matrices already have entries in E by their types; their coordinates need not be adjoined separately.

For any basis b with upper triangular automorphism F, membership in b.flag j means that all coordinates with index at least j vanish. This proves preservation of the initial spans. Basis.span on the restricted independent family gives adapted bases, whose cardinalities are j. Restrict F to each span; its injectivity and finite dimension give LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo. Applying F to the inverse restriction identifies it with F⁻¹. This also proves that F⁻¹ is upper triangular. On the j-th initial span, the j-th coordinate of F x is the j-th diagonal entry times the j-th coordinate of x. Applying this formula to the inverse image of b j shows the diagonal is nonzero. Define α j by Units.mk0.

The last-coordinate linear map on b.flag j.succ has kernel exactly the comap of b.flag j.castSucc and is surjective, with preimage t • b j for t. Its quotient equivalence is obtained from quotEquivOfEq and quotKerEquivOfSurjective. Conjugate multiplication by α j through this equivalence to define g j; the coordinate formula identifies it with the restricted action, and injectivity identifies the inverse. The inclusion is injective, its range is the kernel of mkQ, and mkQ is surjective. Apply the same construction to bΩ and FΩ; the matrix comparison identifies its diagonal units with the images of α.

The canonical inclusion/mkQ sequences over E remain injective, exact and surjective after base change: use Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap, Module.Flat.lTensor_exact and LinearMap.lTensor_surjective, and baseChange_eq_ltensor. Finally Submodule.baseChange_span and map_span identify the initial spans of the transported basis over Ω with the transported base changes. All constructions work also for the empty basis.
